title: Poinsett cucumber (Poinsett 76): Characteristics
metaDescription: Poinsett cucumber is an open pollinated (American slicer) cucumber variety. See its days to harvest, yield, pest ratings, traits and where it grows best.
excerpt: Poinsett cucumber is an open pollinated (American slicer) cucumber variety, also sold or known as Poinsett 76. It is not a registered variety, so the facts here come from its seller and farm sources. It comes from Allied Botanical (Condor), also Ramgo.

blocks.text: If you came here looking for Poinsett 76, this is the same cucumber. The facts below come from its seller and from farm sources, each one listed at the end. Compare it with the others in our [cucumber variety finder](/crop-varieties/cucumber), or see [every crop variety](/crop-varieties) we list. For the crop itself, read our guide: [Land preparation for gourds and melons](/land-preparation/cucurbit-land-preparation).

blocks.text: How long does it take, and how much does it yield?

No day count or trial yield is published for this variety. So ask the seller or your municipal agriculturist for figures from farms near you before you plan a season around it.

Once you know the day count, anee.io dates every task from each lot's own planting day, with [the growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside it.
Is it resistant to pests and diseases?
No pest or disease ratings are published for this variety. So treat it as untested, and scout every week.

The pests and diseases that hit cucumber fields most often: [anthracnose](/diseases/anthracnose), [damping off](/diseases/damping-off), [downy mildew of cucurbits](/diseases/downy-mildew), [leafminer](/pests/leafminer), [melon fly](/pests/melon-fly). Our [pest finder](/pests) and [disease finder](/diseases) help you name what you see.
What its seller and farm sources say

items: **Days to harvest:** First harvest 40 to 45 days after transplanting (Allied), Ramgo gives 50 to 52 days.
**Fruit:** Thick, large, dark green cylinders, Allied's sheet gives about 90 to 100 g.

blocks.text: Why farmers know it: the long standing open pollinated slicer, packed by both Allied Botanical (Poinsett 76) and Ramgo (garden packet). These are the seller's own figures, from its own trials. So plant a small area first, and compare it with your usual cucumber on the same ground.
Where and when to plant Poinsett cucumber

Cucumber gives its first fruit fast, often in five to six weeks. Pick a variety bred to tolerate downy mildew if you plant near the rains. Before planting, get the field ready with our guide: [Pagtatanim ng gulay](/crops/pagtatanim-ng-gulay).

items: Buy sealed packs or tagged sacks from an accredited dealer, and check the packing date and germination rate.
Ask your municipal agriculturist or nearby farmers how it did in your area last season.
Try it on a small area first, beside the variety you usually plant, before you switch the whole farm.
Write down the planting day, inputs and harvest, so you can compare varieties on your own ground. anee.io keeps these records for you.

items.q: Is Poinsett 76 the same as Poinsett?
items.a: Yes. Poinsett 76 is another name for Poinsett. Seed sellers use both, so ask for either one.
Yes. It is open pollinated, so seed from a clean, isolated field grows true. Still, certified seed gives the best start every few seasons.

items.q: Where can I buy seed of Poinsett?
items.a: Ask an accredited seed dealer in your province, the seller named on this page or your municipal agriculturist. Look for the certified seed tag or a sealed pack before you pay.
